articles.title_orig: Base jumper dies in Utah after wingsuit fails in remote mountainous region
articles.title_zh: Base jumper dies in Utah after wingsuit fails in remote mountainous region
articles.content_orig:
A 27-year-old BASE jumper died Sunday after his wingsuit failed when he launched from a 700-foot perch in Utah, authorities said.
The man, whose identity was withheld until his family could be notified, fatally plunged from a mountainous area of Hyrum, Utah, east of Millville Canyon and east of the small city of Millville, Cache County Chief Sheriff’s Deputy Doyle Peck said.
Search-and-rescue crews were called to Leetham’s Hollow, an area of canyon walls and cliffs not unlike the Grand Canyon’s, at 9:10 a.m. Sunday and declared the man dead at the scene, Peck said in a statement.
“On today’s jump, something went wrong and he did not have enough lift with his wingsuit,” Peck said. “He impacted the ground at a high rate of speed resulting in his death.”
The man was “experienced in this type of activity” and was part of a group of as many as 10 people who appeared to be engaged in wingsuit-aided BASE jumping, according to Peck.
The area, about 45 miles north of Ogden, is popular with BASE jumpers, he said.
A medical transport helicopter sent to help with the initial search transported the man’s body, Peck said.
Before Sunday, 541 deaths around the world since 1981 had been logged by the BASE Fatality List , maintained by an online community for the sport. This year, 15 such deaths have been reported globally, according to the list.
In June, two BASE jumpers died in a separate accident in Utah . One of them, Andy Lewis, performed onstage with Madonna at the 2012 Super Bowl.
Photographer Carl Boenish helped coin BASE as a description of the sport’s adrenaline-inspiring launch points (buildings, antennas, spans, earth) in 1978, when he videotaped early jumps from Yosemite National Park’s El Capitan rock formation.
Dennis Romero is a breaking news reporter for NBC News Digital.

articles.title_orig: Russian strikes on Ukraine kill at least 7, including woman at Kyiv's National Academy of Sciences
articles.title_zh: Russian strikes on Ukraine kill at least 7, including woman at Kyiv's National Academy of Sciences
articles.content_orig:
Three others wounded as jet-powered drones increasingly target Ukraine’s capital, with medical centre also hit
Europe live – latest updates
A Russian drone hit the National Academy of Sciences in central Kyiv on Monday, killing at least one person, in the latest daytime attack on Ukraine’s capital.
Flames tore through the historic building as people clambered out of first- and second-floor windows to escape, in dramatic scenes increasingly familiar in the heavily bombarded city.
At least one person was killed and three others were wounded, according to Kyiv’s mayor, Vitali Klitschko , who said the injured had been taken to hospital.
The 19th-century building stands close to the German embassy, the National Opera, St Volodymyr’s Cathedral and several government buildings.
Anatoliy Zagorodny, the president of the national academy, said the blast struck while many staff members were inside. Standing outside the burning building, he said he did not know why Russia had targeted a leading centre of scientific research.
“We are not connected with the military. This is an attack on science. It is terrorism,” he said. He feared some of his colleagues could still be trapped inside the academy.
While the sciences building is a civilian scientific institution, it has longstanding ties to Ukraine’s defence sector. Among those injured in Monday’s strike was Volodymyr Horbulin, the academy’s first vice-president and a former high-ranking security official.
Another Russian drone struck a nearby private medical centre, killing at least one person.
Russian strikes over the past week involving missiles and increasingly sophisticated jet-powered drones have hit apartment blocks, offices, warehouses and datacentres across the capital, killing and wounding civilians almost daily and giving Kyiv an increasingly frontline feel as it faces some of its most sustained bombardment since the early stages of Russia’s full-scale invasion in 2022.
The drone and missile campaign is designed to grind down public resilience and damage the economy. Monday’s double strike is likely to raise fresh concerns over Ukraine’s ability to protect even the most heavily guarded parts of the capital.
The newer jet-powered drones fly faster and are harder to intercept than the older Shahed or Geran-2 models that were the backbone of Moscow’s air campaign. Ukraine is racing to develop and manufacture interceptors capable of bringing them down.
Moscow has also changed its tactics, launching more attacks in daylight hours so that residents in major cities have to spend more of the day under air raid alerts.
after newsletter promotion
Buildings hit during daytime strikes are often occupied because many Ukrainians work through drone alerts rather than spend hours in shelters.
Meanwhile, a Russian jet-powered drone struck western Ukraine near the border crossing with Poland, prompting Warsaw to issue an alert warning of a possible air attack and urging residents in the eastern Lublin region to seek shelter.
Russian forces have increasingly targeted Ukrainian border crossings with Poland and Moldova, leading Kyiv to consider relocating joint customs checkpoints to the territory of neighbouring countries. “It’s again a threat very close to our border,” said Lt Col Jacek Goryszewski, speaking to Poland’s broadcaster TVN24.
Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy , called on western countries to intensify their pressure on Russia. “Every Russian terrorist attack is a loss of life that could have been prevented if pressure on Russia had finally become total,” he wrote on X on Monday. “The world must understand that terrorists will go further if they are not stopped here, in Ukraine. And we cannot turn a blind eye to such brutal strikes.”
Russia has signalled that its attacks on Ukraine could intensify, and US-brokered efforts to end the war show little sign of progress.
“Ukraine will have to pay a price for the actions that have taken place in recent months,” the Kremlin spokesperson, Dmitry Peskov, told reporters on Monday, referring to Ukrainian strikes deep inside Russian territory. “That is happening right now.”

articles.title_orig: Trump asked China’s president if he wanted to buy US arms, ambassador says
articles.title_zh: Trump asked China’s president if he wanted to buy US arms, ambassador says
articles.content_orig:
David Perdue’s remarks come after a Taiwanese minister spoke of the ‘severe’ military threat posed by Beijing to the self-ruled island
Donald Trump offered to sell weapons to China while hosting its leader, Xi Jinping, last week, the US ambassador to China said on Sunday.
David Perdue told Fox News on Sunday: “President Trump continues to say, hey, we sell arms to other people around the world. He actually asked President Xi, would he like to buy some at one point.”
On Monday, Chinese state media praised the “extraordinary level of courtesy” that Trump had shown Xi on the Chinese leader’s visit to Washington .
The extraordinary claim came during an interview about US policy on Taiwan, which has been waiting for months for Trump to approve a new arms sales ⁠package worth $14bn (£10.5bn), after a record multibillion-dollar deal was announced in December last year.
Trump’s level of commitment to protecting Taiwan has previously been questioned . At a meeting with Xi in Beijing in May, ⁠Trump said he was keeping the $14bn Taiwan arms sales package in abeyance, describing it as a “very good negotiating chip” in dealings with China.
Washington has long maintained a strategically ambiguous stance on whether it would defend Taiwan in the event of an invasion. But under the decades-old Taiwan Relations Act, it is required to provide Taipei with sufficient military equipment to defend itself.
Beijing has repeatedly said it “resolutely opposes” Washington’s arms sales to the island democracy, which it regards as a breakaway province, despite never having ruled it, and has not renounced the use of force to take it. During their Washington meeting last week, Xi urged Trump to oppose “Taiwan independence”, according to a readout from the official Chinese news agency Xinhua.
After Perdue’s interview, the White House told the New York Times the US had no plans to sell arms to China , while the state department said: “US law prohibits arms sales to China and there is no offer or plan to sell arms to China.”
China is a net exporter of weapons. Of the arms that it does import, most come from Russia, but the volume is rapidly falling thanks to advances in China’s own military manufacturing capacity. China’s arms imports fell by 72% between 2021 and 2025 compared with the previous five years, according to data from the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute.
Before the interview, the Taiwanese deputy foreign minister, Chen Ming-chi, spoke of the severe military threat China posed.
“Taiwan faces a severe situation in the Taiwan strait. Even though China’s economy is declining, it continues investing more resources into building military capacity. Under ‌this context, the US very much understands our defence needs,” he told reporters in Taipei.
On Sunday, a Taiwanese official, Shen Yu-chung, also pushed back on what he said was an attempt by Beijing to “falsely claim that the Chinese Communist party and the US were allies” in the second world war. A fact sheet released by the White House after the Trump-Xi summit had said China and the US “fought side by side to win” in the war.
China’s government during the second world war was the Republic of China led by Chiang Kai-shek. Chiang’s government fled to Taiwan in 1949 after losing the Chinese civil war to the communists, who established the People’s Republic of China in 1949.
In recent years Taiwan has sought to emphasise its history of fighting alongside western democratic allies as it hopes to bolster international support against aggression from Beijing.
Trump ​has not mentioned the sale ‌since last week’s summit, saying ‌only on Saturday that Xi understands his position on Taiwan.
Perdue told CNBC ​on Friday that there had been ​no change in Taiwan policy by Trump, including on arms ​sales.
Reuters contributed to this report

articles.title_zh: Opinion | China is no longer just the world’s factory. It’s the HQ
articles.content_orig:
Manufacturing capacity is moving overseas but China, as a global hub for innovation and development, remains the ‘industrial brain’
The global electronics industry is entering a structural transition. For over two decades, China served as the dominant manufacturing centre, with an unmatched concentration of suppliers, skilled labour, infrastructure, logistics and engineering capabilities. That concentration is being diluted. But interpreting this as the decline of Chinese manufacturing would be a mistake.
According to the Boston Consulting Group (BCG), since 2017, the share of electronics manufacturers from China – Taiwan, Hong Kong and the mainland – with overseas production has risen to 56 per cent from 12 per cent. BCG based its analysis on 942 publicly traded companies with annual revenues above US$500 million, including 314 headquartered in China. This transformation is remarkable.

articles.title_orig: Why South Korea is demanding an apology from Ukraine over North Korean PoWs
articles.title_zh: Why South Korea is demanding an apology from Ukraine over North Korean PoWs
articles.content_orig:
South Korea has demanded an official apology and explanation from Ukraine after accusing Kyiv of disclosing the transfer of two North Korean prisoners of war to Seoul.
Seong Ghi-hong, senior presidential secretary for public relations, said in a statement on Sunday that the president’s office expressed “strong regret over Ukraine’s unilateral disclosure and its subsequent false announcement that there had not been a non-disclosure agreement”.
He said Ukraine had repeatedly discussed the prisoners’ transfer with Seoul through various channels and had requested secrecy.
However, Kyiv has said no secrecy agreement existed.
Speaking at the annual United Nations General Assembly last week, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Kyiv had transferred two captured North Korean soldiers to South Korea after they were caught fighting for Russia in the Kursk region. Ukraine seized large parts of the Russian border region in August 2024 but has since lost most of the territory.
“These guys are not easy to capture alive. One of them, when he realised he was going to be taken prisoner, tried to kill himself, and he was shocked that fate did not let him die,” Zelenskyy said in his speech.
He also condemned North Korea’s deployment of troops to support Moscow, saying: “This is madness too. Why should Koreans give their lives in a war against Ukraine? [North Korean leader] Kim Jong Un uses them like currency, and he gets something in return.”
Zelenskyy said at the time that he would hand the captured soldiers over to Kim if he could facilitate their exchange for Ukrainians held captive in Russia.
However, human rights groups had urged him to send them to South Korea, referring to possible risks of punishment that the soldiers faced.
South Korean media also reported that the two captured soldiers had wanted to defect to Seoul.
Ukraine captured the two North Koreans in January 2025.
They became the first North Korean soldiers to be captured alive since Pyongyang began in 2024 to aid Moscow’s war efforts against Ukraine. North Korea is estimated to have deployed thousands of soldiers to support Russia’s war against Ukraine as part of a mutual defence treaty .
South Korea previously declined to confirm the soldiers’ arrival, citing concerns about their safety and that of their family members still in North Korea.
But Zelenskyy’s decision to announce the transfer surprised South Korea’s government.
In a post on X, President Lee Jae Myung said the issue of repatriating North Korean prisoners of war was a “highly sensitive agenda”.
“From the perspective of those who advertised the repatriation to the whole world with enthusiastic fanfare to show off their achievements – regardless of the impact on inter-Korean relations, the loss of life, or the damage to national interests – they likely not only cannot understand our government’s efforts to keep it confidential but may even wonder if there is something wrong with it,” Lee wrote.
“I do not know the reasons behind Ukraine’s disclosure in violation of the non-disclosure agreement, but it is deeply regrettable,” he added.
South Korea is technically still at war with North Korea because the two opponents in the 1950-1953 Korean War signed an armistice in 1953 and not a peace treaty. Thousands of US soldiers are stationed in South Korea, and the two allies hold military exercises regularly, which the North has denounced.
According to Seong’s statement on Sunday, Zelenskyy disclosed the repatriation without sufficient prior consultation and later denied that any confidentiality agreement existed.
He added that the denial had seriously damaged trust between the two governments and could harm their relations.
At the same time, opposition politicians have condemned Lee’s government for failing to disclose the transfer.
Last week, opposition politician Ahn Cheol-soo of the People Power Party asked on social media whether it was “fair” that the Korean public learned about North Korean POWs in the country through Zelenskyy.
“President Lee, why did you hide it? Does North Korea have something that, if disclosed, would end your political career? Or were you planning to send the POWs back to North Korea?” Ahn asked.
According to Ukrainian and South Korean estimates, about 14,000 to 15,000 North Korean soldiers were sent to support Russia’s war efforts, and most were deployed to Russia’s Kursk region to fend off a Ukrainian incursion.
As a close Russian ally, Pyongyang has also supplied Moscow with weapons, including artillery and mortar rounds, ballistic missiles, long-range artillery systems and multiple-launch rocket systems, according to Ukrainian and independent assessments.
The soldiers are expected to undergo questioning and security screening before South Korean authorities decide whether to grant them protection and begin resettlement.
On Monday, Seoul’s Ministry of Unification said it would review their cases under relevant laws and past practices, including the North Korean Defectors Protection and Settlement Support Act.
The ministry’s goal is to unify the two Koreas, which were partitioned shortly before the 1950-1953 war. Pyongyang opposes reunification.
Under the law, the National Intelligence Service investigates applicants in temporary protective custody,
Yu Yong-weon, an opposition lawmaker who met the soldiers in Ukraine in February 2025, said they served in North Korea’s special forces and could provide information on Pyongyang’s training, military capabilities and participation in the war.

articles.content_orig:
Benjamin Satterley, an English wrestling star known by his ring name Pac, has died at 40, according to All Elite Wrestling.
“A native of Newcastle upon Tyne, England, Satterley began his wrestling career in 2004 and went on to perform for wrestling organizations all over the world, captivating fans with innovative high-flying moves and incredible in-ring ability,” said AEW in its announcement Sunday night.
“Pac signed with All Elite Wrestling in 2019 and held multiple AEW Championships and competed in some of the most memorable matches in AEW history,” it said, extending condolences to his family, friends and fans.
He previously wrestled for WWE under the ring name Neville, and became known for his aerial attacks and explosive style – earning himself nicknames like “King of the Cruiserweights” and “The Man That Gravity Forgot.”
The circumstances and cause of his death were not provided.
The announcement came just a day after Satterley wrestled a match at AEW’s “All Out” pay-per-view event near Chicago, going up against Andrade El Ídolo.
During his acclaimed career, Satterley made history as the inaugural AEW All-Atlantic Champion in 2022 before the title changed to the AEW International Championship. He was also an acclaimed AEW World Trios Champion, winning the championship alongside teammates Claudio Castagnoli and Wheeler Yuta in front of tens of thousands of fans at Wembley Stadium in his home country in 2024.
Satterley’s death comes just a few weeks after another AEW wrestler, Andy Williams, known professionally as The Butcher, died after collapsing at an independent match in Pennsylvania, according to AEW. He was 48.
Tributes for Satterley have poured in from fans and peers in the wrestling world.
Fellow AEW wrestler Nick Wayne, the youngest champion in AEW history, recalled speaking with Satterley in 2024 after watching him in a match. Satterley’s “conversations, advice, and positive thoughts going into things is something I always cherished,” Wayne wrote on X . “PAC is one of the greatest innovators and Professional Wrestlers to ever do it.”
Will Ospreay, also an English wrestler signed with AEW, who has faced Satterley many times in the ring, posted on X that Satterley was “the greatest export from our country. Also the greatest human being.”
Since joining AEW in 2019, Satterley had wrestled in 147 matches, with 94 wins, 47 losses, and four draws, according to the AEW website.
He also wrestled for Japanese promotions Dragongate and New Japan Pro-Wrestling, as well as the Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre. After the news of his death, New Japan said it was “deeply saddened” by his passing, expressing its sympathies for his friends and family.
CMLL also expressed its condolences, writing on X it will “remember his extraordinary professionalism, dedication, and respect in every appearance in Mexico.”

articles.title_zh: Trevor Lawrence kneeled at the 1-yard line instead of scoring TD, and his explanation makes sense
articles.content_orig:
The Jacksonville Jaguars and New England Patriots ' Week 3 showdown felt like an early taste of the AFC Playoffs when the 2026 schedule was announced. Just a few weeks into the new season, these two teams already seem headed in opposite directions: the Jags feel like a rising Super Bowl contender with a stud quarterback, while the Patriots are experiencing the dreaded Super Bowl hangover as Drake Maye continues to regress against a tougher schedule .
The Jaguars beat the Patriots, 35-6, on Sunday in a dominant performance across all four quarters. Maye was horrendous for New England , turning the ball over three times and looking like a broken quarterback throughout the game. Meanwhile, Trevor Lawrence quietly executed the Jacksonville offense at a high level, finishing with three passing touchdowns and one interception while adding 182 yards through the air.
Lawrence could have had another touchdown during the fourth quarter, but he decided to take a knee instead. On a designed run, Lawrence broke multiple tackles at the line of scrimmage to find a clear path to the end zone. Instead of running it in, he opted to take a knee, which felt incredibly odd in the moment because there was nearly nine minutes left in the game. NFL fans watching the game were super confused at what just happened. Watch the play here:
Why didn't Lawrence just score? It was only a three possession game with about nine minutes left, which is way too much time to start bleeding the clock. Imagine if the Jags fumbled on the next play, or if Lawrence somehow threw a pick-six from the end zone.
Lawrence joked after the game that he just wanted to get teammate Bhayshul Tuten a touchdown for his fantasy owners . Tuten ended up scoring on the very next play. It was a good line, but it took until the postgame press conference for him to admit what actually happened.
Lawrence said after the game that he was trying to bleed clock, but he probably made a mistake. "When I broke free and nobody tackled me, it's something we talk about all the time potentially, going down and keeping the clock running. That was too much time (left to take a knee). … It probably wasn't the best decision." Watch Lawrence's full explanation here:
This felt like a mistake in the moment. It's refreshing to hear Lawrence admit he screwed up.
Lawrence probably could have done his offensive line a favor by just scoring rather than making them line up for a highly physical goal line snap. In the end, Tuten scored, and the Jags rolled.
No one is going to remember this moment in a few weeks, and that's just the way Lawrence wanted it.

Here are the highlights from the 2026 VMAs.
Madonna took the VMAs stage at the Peacock Theater in downtown Los Angeles, her first time performing at the award show in over 20 years, announcing: "It's mother."
She opened the show with newly iconic imagery from her recent album, "Confessions II," including green lasers and hordes of cameras following her and Sabrina Carpenter around.
The two performed "Bring Your Love" together, which later won the Best Collaboration award, before Madonna transitioned into another dance-fueled club number, "Danceteria," with Charli XCX. Madonna later took home Artist of the Year.
Kacey Musgraves paid tribute to Dolly Parton on Sunday after the VMAs played a short video of the late country music superstar. Musgraves sang "I Will Always Love You," a song Parton released in 1974 that took on a second life when it was later recorded by the late Whitney Houston.
Parton, one of the most groundbreaking and successful musicians in the history of country music, died last month after a brief battle with cancer.

articles.title_zh: US and China release reciprocal $30 billion product lists for tariff cuts after Trump-Xi meeting
articles.content_orig:
The United States and China have agreed to slash tariffs on $60 billion worth of goods, deepening efforts to stabilize a frequently testy relationship.
The tariff relief extends to an array of products, from US coal and agricultural products to made-in-China toys, car seats and holiday decorations.
The announcement from the White House late Sunday followed a highly anticipated meeting between US President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Washington last week.
The White House said that under a so-called “30-for-30” framework, each country would be allowed to import “non-sensitive” goods worth $30 billion from the other at reduced tariff rates.
The more favorable tariff treatment followed recommendations from the US-China Board of Trade and would improve market access for about 30% of US exports to China, US trade representative Jamieson Greer said in a statement Sunday.
The Trump-Xi meeting was heavy on pomp, light on substance. China is just fine with that
“The Trump Administration will continue to pursue fair, balanced, and reciprocal trade with China by ensuring compliance with commitments on agricultural and energy purchases, pursuing balanced trade in non-sensitive goods, and securing market access for American farmers, manufacturers, businesses, and workers,” he added.
The Chinese list of US products that will be subject to lower tariffs covers 1,619 items, including corn, wheat, frozen meat, seafood, wood products, cosmetics and medical devices, according to a list published by the White House . US soybeans were not included, a blow to struggling American farmers who have been collateral damage from a years-long tit-for-tat trade war between the two countries.
The White House also said that China would import at least 10 million metric tons of coal from the United States in 2027 and again in 2028. Previous commitments to import certain quantities of goods, such as agricultural products, have not always been met in full, however.
The US list of Chinese imports covers 77 items, including toys, tableware, kitchen accessories, curtains, electric shavers and inflatable balls.
The Chinese commerce ministry said the agreement would “further stabilize” China-US economic and trade relations and “create favorable conditions” for the export of relevant Chinese products to the United States.
The announcement comes after the US and China agreed ahead of Xi’s visit to press pause on escalating tariff measures until January 10. The trade truce – which sets tariff levels at 30% on Chinese goods and 10% on US goods – has been extended multiple times since May 2025, when the two countries met in Geneva for negotiations.
The goods listed Sunday, however, will likely be carved out of future tariff measures.
Trump has used tariffs to narrow the US trade deficit with China – or the difference between what America exports to China and what it imports from China – prompting Chinese exporters to send more goods elsewhere, including to Europe.
In an interview with CNBC on Friday, Greer said the deficit on goods trade with China had fallen 40% since Trump took office and was on track to reach $140 billion this year. Data from the US Census Bureau showed the deficit amounted to around $295 billion in 2024.
Beyond trade, the two countries also agreed to establish a bilateral communication channel to discuss any artificial intelligence-related “incidents,” according to the White House.
The White House said Xi and Trump agreed to use the term “super intelligence” rather than “artificial intelligence” to describe the emerging technology, and that the two sides had established the. U.S.-China Super Intelligence Dialogue to exchange views on risks and benefits related to AI. The next exchange will occur by November 2026.

articles.title_zh: Madonna’s ‘Danceteria’ Was One of the Great Moments in VMAs History
articles.content_orig:
Madonna made her big return to the MTV Video Music Awards, her first time at the annual event in 23 years. She practically invented this show the very first time it aired in 1984, making her infamous debut in her white wedding gown as the scandalous floor-humping bride in “Like a Virgin.” That performance did wonders for her, but even bigger wonders for the VMAs —it’s the moment this event has always aspired to match ever since. It established her as the once and future queen of this show. But strange as it seems, until last night, she hadn’t rocked the VMAs since 2003, when she did an even better version of “Like a Virgin,” in her legendary make out session with Britney Spears .
So the stakes were high for her hotly-anticipated return last night. But her amazing performance with Sabrina Carpenter and Charli XCX stole the show, with a medley of “One Step Away,” “Bring Your Love,” and “Danceteria,” from her recent Confessions II. It wasn’t just the highlight of the night; it was one of the most stunning performances in the entire history of the VMAs, hands down.
It’s fitting that she began with Sabrina, who was just four years old when Madonna smooched Britney, but a quintessential Daughter of the House of Ciccone. “It’s mother,” a voice moaned at the beginning, as Madonna recited her disco catechism. “The dance floor is not a place,” she said. “It’s a threshold. A ritualistic space where movement replaces language.”
#SabrinaCarpenter makes a surprise appearance during #Madonna ’s #VMAs performance. (via CBS/MTV/VMAs) pic.twitter.com/b7UtSqEilT
Wearing a black beret, Sabrina played the piano with Madonna writhing on top of it. They did their Coachella-slaying duet “Bring Your Love,” with Sabrina twisting and crawling in her glitter-spangled black liederhosen. Madonna wrestled with black-clad storm troopers, then got rolled on a gurney through the crowd, until a really confusing interlude where she met a bizarro alien gospel choir in white gowns. (A very Creed touch.)
But the performance really exploded when Charli XCX strutted in for “Danceteria,” as the stage transformed into the famous early-Eighties NYC disco, with the cool girls hanging out in the men’s room. Charli even stroked the bathroom hand-dryer—a clever reference to everybody’s favorite scene in Desperately Seeking Susan .
CHARLI XCX PERFORMING ‘DANCETERIA AFTERHOURS’ WITH MADONNA pic.twitter.com/LbLrourkag
The “Danceteria” bathroom was jumping with party people. Over here, Madonna and Charli rocking out. Over there, Sombr posing as a scantily clad black-leather boy. Hey, look—it’s Debi Mazar, years before Goodfellas , just another party girl and Madonna’s coolest club-kid girlfriend, name-checked in the song. (Also, a callback to Debi’s cameo in the “Music” video from Y2K—maybe Madonna’s peak era ever?) Hey, that guy looks like…wait, it is Fab 5 Freddy, also namechecked. Julia Garner, dressed in the “Open Your Heart” black corset and haircut. Tony Ward, from the “Justify My Love” video. The “Boy Toy” belt buckle. Producer Andrew Watt, as Keith Haring. Seth Rogen … wait, really? What the hell is Seth doing here? Who dragged him to a disco? Ah, well—everybody’s welcome here. Anyone can be a star on Madonna’s dance floor. That’s the whole point of the song—as she keeps chanting, “Everybody here is a work of art.”
A clever detail: Lou Reed’s face on the “Danceteria” bathroom wall, the Mick Rock photo from the cover of his 1972 classic Transformer , as they all sang the “doo de doo de doo” hook from “Walk on the Wild Side.” (Watt walked the red carpet in a t-shirt displaying that Lou photo.) Given my unfortunately encyclopedic memory for trashy award shows, I can tell you this was Lou’s first cameo on the VMAs since 2006, when he and Jack White played “White Light/White Heat” with the Raconteurs.
Madonna made it all feel like a musical autobiography for her, doubling as a capsule history of club culture. It summed up where she came from, why she left, why she came to New York, and what she made of the dreams she worked to bring to life. That’s the theme of her excellent album Confessions II . But she packed the whole messy story into “Danceteria.” Related Content The VMAs: The One Night When MTV Pretends to be MTV Taylor Swift Pays Tribute to Dolly Parton While Accepting Video of the Year Award at 2026 VMAs GENER8ION and Yung Lean Premiere Electrifying Performance of ‘Storm II’ at 2026 VMAs Raye, Sombr, Teddy Swims, Adam Lambert Salute  George Michael at MTV VMAs
Madonna kept winning awards all night, giving magnificently chaotic, unprepared, and awkward speeches, yet still with more star power than anyone in the room. Her best moment: when she won the Best Dance category, threw her arms around Charli and Troye Sivan, and said, “I’m kind of unclear what this award is for?” You and us both, Madonna. Charli had to re-read the envelope to confirm it was for her Confessions II short film. She complained about the mic stand being too high for her. She also did one of the most uncomfortable dad jokes ever heard on an award show, including the ones hosted by Billy Crystal: “First of all, I’d like to thank my fingers, because I can always count on them.” Why in God’s name did she say this? Madonna, you’re on live TV here. Hold it together. We’re rooting for you.
But even when she was making everyone squirm (poor Troye looked terrified), she was still the coolest, and she knew it, fully confident this was her show. She told the story of her 1984 “Like a Virgin” moment, and how her management team told her backstage that she’d just killed her career. “My dress went up, and my buttcheek was hanging out,” she recalled. “And in those days, buttcheeks were not hanging out.” When she and Sabrina won for Best Collaboration with “Bring Your Love,” she complained about how Sabrina’s handlers waited to return her call, until Sabrina got bleeped for quipping, “My team is shitting themselves backstage.” But she generously spent her speech heaping praise on Sabrina. “She has OCD and so do I,” Madonna said. “We write our lyrics down on pieces of paper, like they did in the 1800s.” Sabrina simply said, “Everybody, Madonna,” before they walked off hand in hand. Trending Stories U2 Dream It All Up Again Madonna’s ‘Danceteria’ Was One of the Great Moments in VMAs History Raye, Sombr, Teddy Swims, Adam Lambert Salute George Michael at MTV VMAs How Trump Became Mob Boss of the United States
THIS DUO!!! @Madonna and @SabrinaAnnLynn take home Best Collaboration at the #VMAs 👯‍♀️🏆 pic.twitter.com/YMlwumHuTd
But the most poignant moment came when Madonna recalled where songs like “Danceteria” came from. “I came to New York to be a dancer,” she said. “Dance is where everything happened for me in my life. I came to life on the dance floor. I found my community on the dance floor. I fell in love with people on the dance floor. And I lost many people I loved on the dance floor.” It was a powerful confession. “Dance brings everybody together, okay?” she said. “We are all equal on the dance floor.” You couldn’t ask for a more succinct summary of everything Madonna’s VMAs performance—or her entire career—has been about.
I’ve been a Madonna fan—and an MTV junkie—since the early days. I’ve seen every VMAs from the beginning, since the night she debuted with “Like a Virgin,” rolling on the floor in her bridal gown, with her rosary beads and Boy Toy belt buckle. So I’m used to seeing Madonna steal the show, year after year—with her glam “Express Yourself” in 1989, her Marie Antoinette-style “Vogue” in 1990, her “Ray of Light” with Lenny Kravitz in 1998. Not to mention her infamously rowdy rooftop interview at the 1995 VMAs, throwing shade with Courtney Love and Kurt Loder. Give Madonna a few minutes of live MTV and she’ll always find a way to seize the moment. But this performance—especially the “Danceteria” half—was so emotional, so deeply personal, so elegiac, yet without sacrificing any of the disco sleaze or body-electric jubilati

British counterterrorism police are leading an investigation after five men were arrested on suspicion of explosives offenses and preparing a terrorist act near an air base used by U.S. forces.
Police received a report at around 12:45 a.m. Sunday about three suspicious vehicles traveling toward RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire, southwestern England. Armed officers responded and arrested the men in nearby Whelford.
Fairford is used as a forward operating location for the U.S. Air Force Global Strike Command. The base has hosted U.S. B-52 and B-1 bombers during the Iran war , according to ABC News . American forces have used Fairford to carry out strikes against Iranian missile sites, the Associated Press reported.
Read More: Why More Republicans Are Breaking With Trump on Iran
In a press conference Sunday, Assistant Chief Constable Richard Ocone said that about 85 households in the area were advised to evacuate early Sunday morning as a precaution.
"A 400m cordon has been put in place around the vehicles, while the Army's Explosive Ordnance Disposal Unit examine them,” Ocone said. A statement from police earlier Sunday said that they believe the situation is “contained.”
Aerial footage from Sky News shows a bomb disposal robot moving between three white vans at the site, with the rear doors of two vehicles open.
Ocone added that the men remain in custody and will be questioned by police.
The base is home to both the 501st Combat Support Wing Headquarters and the 420th Air Base Squadron, and serves as the “preferred bomber forward operating location in Europe,” according to the U.S. Air Force.
TIME has reached out to the U.S. Air Force for comment on the incident.
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who assumed the post in July, called the incident “deeply concerning” on X .
“The safety and security of the public is our first priority, and I want people to know that we will always take every step necessary to protect our communities and keep our country safe,” he wrote. “The investigation remains ongoing, and I would urge people not to speculate while the authorities establish the full facts.” When asked by reporters about the arrests, U.S. President Donald Trump called them “fantastic.” “They were looking to do big damage to our fort,” Trump said of the suspects, “and working with the British worked out great.”
Trump also said the suspects had been under surveillance before their arrests. “We had them under view for a long time, and we got them,” he said.
British police have not confirmed that RAF Fairford was the intended target of the suspected attacks. The Associated Press reported that investigators were considering a possible connection to Iran, but no such link has been confirmed.

(Kitco News) – China’s 2026 gold imports could be double those of last year, and will set the high-water mark for the 2020s to date, while silver prices are approaching a key test that could determine the gray metal’s near-term direction, according to precious metals analysts at Heraeus.
In their latest update, the analysts noted that China’s gold imports have already exceeded 2025 totals in 2026. “China imported 142 tonnes of gold in August, taking imports during the first eight months of the year to 1,141 tonnes, 72% higher than the 663 tonnes imported over the same period last year, and higher than the 940 tonnes imported during the whole of 2025,” they wrote. “The strong inflows come despite historically high gold prices and reflect continued investment demand, while Chinese jewellery demand remains comparatively weak. These non-monetary imports are separate from purchases by the People’s Bank of China, which added a further 20 tonnes to its official reserves in August.”
“If Chinese gold imports maintain this pace through the rest of 2026, they will total ~1,700 tonnes, which would represent the highest amount this decade.”
Australia’s gold mine production continued to rise in fiscal year 2025-26 as historically high prices continue to support the mining sector. “Australia produced 303 tonnes of gold up to the end of its financial year in June, broadly in line with its long-run production rate of around 300 tonnes p.a.,” the analysts said. “Output improved at most operations during the June quarter, while several smaller producers also began production. The 303 tonnes produced in Australia account for around 8% of total mined gold supply, which was 3,822 tonnes in 2025.”
Heraeus said Indonesia is proposing a scheme to incentivize privately held gold stocks to be invested into the formal financial system. “The government estimates that households hold around 1,800 tonnes of gold outside formal investment channels and has asked state-owned institutions to encourage around 20% of this metal, equivalent to roughly 360 tonnes, into bullion-banking and financial products,” they wrote. “The initiative is aimed at turning privately held metal into deposits, collateral and other financial assets, deepening the domestic bullion market and potentially increasing the amount of household wealth circulating through the financial system.”
The analysts also warned that India’s weak monsoon will likely depress rural gold demand during this year’s festival and wedding season – and rural demand represents over 50% of the country’s total bullion consumption. “Monsoon rainfall was around 15% below its long-run average by late September, presenting a downside risk to gold demand due to the potential of lower crop yields to impact rural incomes,” they said. “Historical analysis by the World Gold Council suggests that a 1% increase in rainfall relative to the average is associated with a 0.2% increase in gold demand, implying that this year’s rainfall deficit could represent a modest headwind. Indian gold demand totalled 768 tonnes in 2025, roughly 15% of global demand.”
Spot gold was continuing to test session lows early in the North American session, and last traded at $4,142.30 for a loss of 3.33% on the daily chart.
Turning to silver, Heraeus analysts noted that the renewed strength of the U.S. dollar has driven silver prices to a key inflection point.
“Silver prices dropped below $65/oz last week as the dollar index rose back above 101.0, towards its yearly highs,” they noted. “This leaves silver at an important level. A renewed rally back towards $70/oz despite a rising dollar, a hawkish Federal Reserve and rising bond yields could signal a confirmation of a potential bottoming process. However, if silver falls back below $60/oz, this could be the sign of a continuation of the bearish downtrend, marked by lower highs and lower lows, in which silver has been stuck since its late January peak.”
The analysts wrote that the 10-year Treasury yield’s rise to 5.22% and the 10-year Treasury Inflation-Protected Security (TIPS) real yield hitting 2.8% indicates that the Federal Reserve’s 25 basis point rate hike in September was not enough to reassure markets.
“The rise in real yields alongside nominal yields is particularly significant for precious metals, indicating that the sell-off in Treasuries has not been driven solely by higher inflation expectations, but also by investors demanding a higher inflation-adjusted return, consistent with the anticipation that monetary policy could remain tighter for longer,” they said. “This comes as Brent crude remains around $100/bbl, and despite renewed talks between the US and Iran, a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz does not appear imminent.”
And Indian silver imports spiked higher in August after several months of weak inflows. “India imported 15.5 moz of silver in August, the first time since February that monthly imports have topped 10 moz and 36% higher than the 11.4 moz imported in August 2025,” the analysts wrote. “Despite the strong monthly recovery, imports remain weak for the year as a whole, with an estimated 75.6 moz imported during January-August, 24% less than the 99.1 moz imported over the same period last year.”
“The rebound follows several months of unusually low imports after the licensing requirements introduced in May complicated the import process and high silver prices reduced demand, they said. “The upswing in August suggests that physical inflows are beginning to normalise, although year-to-date imports remain well below last year’s levels.”
Silver prices were also trading just above their earlier session lows on Monday morning after dipping below $61 per ounce around 5 am ET.
Spot silver last traded at $61.302 per ounce for a loss of 4.67% on the daily chart.

Benjamin Satterley, an English wrestling star known by his ring name Pac, has died at 40, according to All Elite Wrestling.
“A native of Newcastle upon Tyne, England, Satterley began his wrestling career in 2004 and went on to perform for wrestling organizations all over the world, captivating fans with innovative high-flying moves and incredible in-ring ability,” said AEW in its announcement Sunday night.
“Pac signed with All Elite Wrestling in 2019 and held multiple AEW Championships and competed in some of the most memorable matches in AEW history,” it said, extending condolences to his family, friends and fans.
He previously wrestled for WWE under the ring name Neville, and became known for his aerial attacks and explosive style – earning himself nicknames like “King of the Cruiserweights” and “The Man That Gravity Forgot.”
The circumstances and cause of his death were not provided.
The announcement came just a day after Satterley wrestled a match at AEW’s “All Out” pay-per-view event near Chicago, going up against Andrade El Ídolo.
During his acclaimed career, Satterley made history as the inaugural AEW All-Atlantic Champion in 2022 before the title changed to the AEW International Championship. He was also an acclaimed AEW World Trios Champion, winning the championship alongside teammates Claudio Castagnoli and Wheeler Yuta in front of tens of thousands of fans at Wembley Stadium in his home country in 2024.
Satterley’s death comes just a few weeks after another AEW wrestler, Andy Williams, known professionally as The Butcher, died after collapsing at an independent match in Pennsylvania, according to AEW. He was 48.
Tributes for Satterley have poured in from fans and peers in the wrestling world.
Fellow AEW wrestler Nick Wayne, the youngest champion in AEW history, recalled speaking with Satterley in 2024 after watching him in a match. Satterley’s “conversations, advice, and positive thoughts going into things is something I always cherished,” Wayne wrote on X . “PAC is one of the greatest innovators and Professional Wrestlers to ever do it.”
Will Ospreay, also an English wrestler signed with AEW, who has faced Satterley many times in the ring, posted on X that Satterley was “the greatest export from our country. Also the greatest human being.”
Since joining AEW in 2019, Satterley had wrestled in 147 matches, with 94 wins, 47 losses, and four draws, according to the AEW website.
He also wrestled for Japanese promotions Dragongate and New Japan Pro-Wrestling, as well as the Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre. After the news of his death, New Japan said it was “deeply saddened” by his passing, expressing its sympathies for his friends and family.
CMLL also expressed its condolences, writing on X it will “remember his extraordinary professionalism, dedication, and respect in every appearance in Mexico.”

The announcement comes after the US and China agreed ahead of Xi’s visit to press pause on escalating tariff measures until January 10. The trade truce – which sets tariff levels at 30% on Chinese goods and 10% on US goods – has been extended multiple times since May 2025, when the two countries met in Geneva for negotiations.
The goods listed Sunday, however, will likely be carved out of future tariff measures.
Trump has used tariffs to narrow the US trade deficit with China – or the difference between what America exports to China and what it imports from China – prompting Chinese exporters to send more goods elsewhere, including to Europe.
In an interview with CNBC on Friday, Greer said the deficit on goods trade with China had fallen 40% since Trump took office and was on track to reach $140 billion this year. Data from the US Census Bureau showed the deficit amounted to around $295 billion in 2024.

articles.title_zh: Mike Vrabel voices ‘very high concern’ after Patriots loss to Jaguars
articles.content_orig:
Penalties and turnovers plagued New England in a 35-6 loss on Sunday.
After a Marcus Jones interception early in the second quarter awarded the New England Patriots a new set of downs at the Jacksonville Jaguars’ 21-yard line, trailing 7-0, the Patriots offense unraveled before they could run a full play.
On first down, right tackle Morgan Moses was called for a holding penalty that wiped out a Drake Maye scrambling touchdown. Then, a Romeo Doubs offensive pass interference call quickly followed that mishap, pushing New England back to a 1st-and-30 possession and forcing the offense to settle for a field goal.
That sequence was an early glimpse of the sloppy, undisciplined football on Sunday afternoon that plagued the Patriots in their dismal 35-6 road loss to the Jaguars.
“My concern level is very high for this football team,” head coach Mike Vrabel said after the contest. “When you come off a game like that, you just want to get back to work … We have to fix a lot of things.”
New England committed nine penalties throughout the matchup. While Jacksonville wasn’t far behind with seven of its own, the Patriots repeatedly made mistakes that prevented them from capitalizing on the Jaguars’ shortcomings.
Trailing just before halftime, but with a larger disparity at 14-3, Maye and his unit had an opportunity to at least cut the game to one score with a third-and-goal snap two yards out from the end zone. However, instead of settling for another three points, the quarterback forced a throw to a smothered Efton Chism III in the back of the painted area, allowing Jacksonville cornerback Travis Hunter to intercept the pass.
Maye was responsible for all three of New England’s turnovers stemming from poor decision-making when dropping back to pass and a jarring fumble that slipped from his hand on a pass attempt.
Still, Vrabel believes that resolving those mistakes begins with himself.
“We haven’t made good decisions with the football,” Vrabel added. “We have to get it fixed. We have to practice. We have to work and get it corrected. And everybody else has to do much better, and it starts with me. That’s how it goes … I need to get guys in there to do the things the way that we need them done.
“There are going to be mistakes, but there are too many things that get us beat: turnovers and not taking advantage of [Jacksonville’s] turnover opportunities.”
Following Maye’s final interception in the third frame, the team’s body language noticeably shifted, with the defense losing its physicality as the game progressed and the offense continuously failing to score.
That body language was evident at all three levels. After the Jaguars extended their lead to 28-3, Kyle Williams, instead of letting the ball roll out of bounds on the ensuing kickoff to accept a penalty, caught the kick, pinning the Patriots at their own nine.
“I think it’s one day at a time,” Vrabel said. “It’s about what we can do to get healthy and improve individually and as a football team. That’s all we can do. It’s going to start with me and my ability to teach and get the guys in the right spots.”
New England, dropping to 1-2 on the season, will travel to Buffalo next week to face the undefeated Bills in a crucial divisional game.

Ted Kaczynski was 16 when he entered Harvard University as a mathematics prodigy. Years later, he would become known as the Unabomber, after carrying out a bombing campaign that killed three people and injured 23 others between 1978 and 1995.
Netflix’s Unabomber directed by Janus Metz, explores Kaczynski’s life before and during the events that led to his capture. Jacob Tremblay plays the younger Kaczynski, while Russell Crowe portrays Harvard professor Henry Murray, Shailene Woodley plays FBI agent Joanne Miller and Annabelle Wallis portrays Christiana Morgan, Murray’s academic collaborator.
“We decided to explore Ted Kaczynski's time at Harvard, as it stood out as a formative and fragile period in his life,” Metz tells TIME. “We wanted to understand who this young man was up until he began his descent into a darker and deadlier path.”
Born in Chicago in 1942, Kaczynski demonstrated exceptional mathematical ability from an early age. He entered Harvard at 16 before continuing his studies at the University of Michigan, where he earned a master’s degree and a doctorate in mathematics.
At 25, he became a professor at the University of California, Berkeley. But he left the university in 1969 and eventually moved to a remote cabin near Lincoln, Mont., where he lived without electricity or running water.
Kaczynski became increasingly isolated from society. He spent much of his time reading, hunting and growing plants, while developing increasingly strong opposition to modern technology and industrial society.
In 1978, Kaczynski began the bombing campaign that would eventually span nearly two decades. His first known attack involved a homemade device mailed to a professor at Northwestern University. It exploded when opened by a campus security officer, causing minor injuries. In November 1979, Kaczynski placed a device aboard an American Airlines flight, causing smoke inhalation injuries and forcing the plane to make an emergency landing.
Over the years, his targets included universities, airlines and people he associated with technology and the modern industrial system.
The FBI used the case identifier UNABOM, short for “University and Airline Bombing,” before Kaczynski’s identity was known. The media later used it to name him the “Unabomber.” Between 1978 and 1995, 16 attacks were linked to the case, killing Hugh Scrutton, Thomas Mosser and Gilbert Murray and injuring 23 people.
Kaczynski’s identity remained a mystery for years. That changed in 1995, when he sent a lengthy manifesto titled “Industrial Society and Its Future”  to The Washington Post and The New York Times and demanded that it be published. The approximately 35,000-word text laid out his opposition to modern technological society and explored ideas about human freedom, autonomy, and the effects of industrialization.
The FBI supported the decision to publish the manifesto in the hope that someone familiar with Kaczynski’s writing would recognize it. That person turned out to be his brother David’s wife, Linda Patrik.
After reading the manifesto, Patrik noticed similarities between its ideas and the writing she had previously seen from Kaczynski. She brought her concerns to David, who initially struggled to believe that his brother could be responsible for the attacks.
David eventually examined the manifesto alongside an essay Kaczynski had written years earlier. The similarities in their language and ideas were striking enough for him to contact the FBI.
The material gave investigators a crucial lead. After years of attacks and an extensive investigation, Kaczynski was now directly connected to the manifesto and the writings that could help identify him as the person behind the Unabomber case.
Shailene Woodley in Unabomber Courtesy of Netflix
On April 3, 1996, nearly two decades after the first attack, federal agents surrounded Kaczynski’s remote cabin near Lincoln, Mont., and arrested him.
The search of the property gave investigators a trove of evidence. Inside, they found bomb-making materials, a typewriter, coded diary entries and approximately 40,000 pages of handwritten notes, along with a completed bomb.
Kaczynski later pleaded guilty and was sentenced to life in prison without parole. He remained incarcerated until his death in 2023 at age 81.
While in prison, Kaczynski was diagnosed with paranoid schizophrenia by a psychiatrist who interviewed him. He rejected the idea that he was mentally incapable of understanding his actions. In a 1999 interview with TIME , he said he was certain he was sane.
While at Harvard, Kaczynski took part in psychological experiments overseen by professor Henry Murray. Murray worked with Christiana Morgan at the Harvard Psychological Clinic, where they developed the Thematic Apperception Test, or TAT.
“Christiana was the co-creator of the Harvard school of psychology where the tests on Ted Kaczynski took place,” says Wallis, who plays Morgan in the movie. “Murray and Morgan were collaborators at the time and together devised the highly controversial stress tests used on Harvard students. I was fascinated to learn about the extent of her involvement.”
The experiments involved students writing about their beliefs before undergoing intense psychological sessions. They later became an important part of discussions about Kaczynski’s life, although their precise impact on him remains uncertain.
The full Harvard file on Kaczynski remains classified, making it impossible to know exactly what Murray concluded from the experiments.
“I don't think the Murray experiments in themselves turned Ted Kaczynski into the Unabomber,” says Metz. “There are many factors in Ted Kaczynski's life that contributed to his evolution.”
However, Metz says the experiments were designed to break down participants who knew very little about what they were being subjected to, and that the filmmakers wanted to show them as “likely a piece of the puzzle.”
Metz also points to Kaczynski’s own writings as another part of the story.
“We also know from Ted Kaczynski's own journals that he wanted revenge from feeling disrespected and rejected, which these experiments could have contributed to,” he says.
According to Metz, Kaczynski himself later claimed that the experiments had not had a significant effect on him.
Russell Crowe and Jacob Tremblay in Unabomber Courtesy of Netflix
For Tremblay, one of the challenges of playing Kaczynski was the lack of detailed information about his early life.
“While there is plenty of information to go off of from Ted's adult life, it was challenging to find material regarding his early life when I played him,” Tremblay says. “I was left with a rather blank canvas in terms of how much freedom I would have with the character.”
Tremblay listened to recordings of Kaczynski’s interrogation after his arrest to study his speech patterns and watched footage of him as an adult, noting his stiff posture. I then put my own youthful, nervous and softer spin on that,” Tremblay says.
The psychological experiment scenes presented a different challenge. Tremblay was strapped to a chair, limiting his movement and expressions. “I learned to utilize that unfamiliar and uncomfortable environment to my advantage,” Tremblay says. “Because Ted himself in that moment is also experiencing that discomfort and unfamiliarity at the same time.”
Unabomber is grounded in documented events from Kaczynski’s life, but the film also takes creative liberties with gaps in the historical record.

articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Nvidia ( NVDA ) released the Open Agent Safety Platform, which is aimed at helping AI developers enforce safeguards for agents, a few days after the AI hardware giant's CEO questioned the security approaches of Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) and OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ).
"AI's extraordinary potential for society will only be realized if we solve AI safety," Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang stated in a press release. "As we continue to discover the frontier of AI capabilities, we must accelerate discovery at the frontier of AI safety. Safety and security require full-stack engineering."
Last week, Huang sat down with Ezra Klein of The New York Times to discuss recent warnings from Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman suggesting that the pace of AI development could threaten humanity.
"If your product is not ready to ship, don't ship the product," Huang told The Ezra Klein Show podcast. "This is the first time that I've heard a company or CEO say that I need … the liability laws of products to be relieved so that I can pace myself."
Huang repeatedly described the stance of the leading AI labs as "odd," given that those companies are leading AI innovation while the safety risks, in his view, can be mitigated with technology.
"Nobody is building more compute today than the people asking to be slowed down," Huang told Klein. "It strikes me as odd. … I know a lot of people in those two labs who are dedicating their lives to do good work. They know what happened. I know they know what happened. I know they know how to fix it, and I know they're fixing it."
Read more: AI isn't coming to destroy humanity, but experts say the real threats are here
The new safety platform is aimed at establishing security protocols that could prevent alarming breaches from being unveiled by the frontier labs.
"NVIDIA Open Agent Safety Platform brings together industry, researchers and public-sector organizations to share best practices, align on evaluation methods and foster international cooperation," Huang added in the press release. "Together, we can raise the bar for global AI safety."
Speaking with Klein, Huang suggested that the AI labs simply rebalance their priorities.
"So when I say we need to accelerate AI technology, people think, for some reason, that safety is not part of that," the Nvidia CEO said . "Safety is part of it. Alignment is part of it. Evaluation is part of it: Guardrailing, sandboxing, the isolation technology, monitoring technology, telemetry technology, external A.I. monitor technology — all of that stuff is A.I. technology. Accelerate the living daylights out of that."
Klein noted that "if the most alarmed people at the labs could be assured they were going to move 80 percent of their compute into safety and alignment, as opposed to 80 percent into capability expansion, they would feel much better."
Huang replied: "Yeah, what's stopping them from doing it?"

articles.title_orig: Israel’s Netanyahu made a secret visit to the UAE on Sunday, source says
articles.title_zh: Israel’s Netanyahu made a secret visit to the UAE on Sunday, source says
articles.content_orig:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu secretly visited the United Arab Emirates on Sunday and met with the country’s president, Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed, an Israeli source familiar with the visit told CNN.
The source said Iran dominated the agenda, an arena where the two countries have deepened their cooperation, including during the current Iran war.
The Israeli Prime Minister’s Office did not confirm the visit. CNN reached out to the UAE foreign ministry for comment.
The rare trip, if confirmed, comes exactly one month before Israel’s October 27 election and against the backdrop of heightened political controversy in Israel over reporting by Haaretz and The New York Times alleging that Bin Zayed had warned Netanyahu of a major Hamas operation days before the October 7, 2023, attack.
The Atlantic separately reported that Egypt’s intelligence chief Abbas Kamel flew to Israel on September 26, 2023, to warn that Gaza would “blow up.” And on Sunday, The Wall Street Journal reported that there were at least three Egyptian warnings conveyed to Israel about Gaza, the last one in a phone call to Netanyahu, just days before the attack.
Netanyahu’s office has repeatedly denied receiving any warning and has dismissed the reports as fabricated lies aimed at damaging him electorally. But his rivals have used the allegations to make accountability for the failure to prevent the October 7, 2023, attack a central campaign issue.
After initial reports of a warning from Bin Zayed , the UAE’s Foreign Ministry said earlier this month that it “does not comment on media stories or speculation regarding conversations between government leaders,” but it did not deny the call. “When necessary, all relevant intelligence has been and continues to be communicated between the relevant entities,” the statement said.
At the time, an Israeli source familiar with the matter said Netanyahu’s office tried to get the UAE to deny the report, but the UAE only agreed to issue a statement about intelligence sharing.
Netanyahu’s Likud party subsequently issued a statement, posted on the prime minister’s X account, alleging “blatant foreign interference” in Israel’s elections by UAE-based Palestinian politician Mohammed Dahlan. The party provided no evidence for the claim.
Netanyahu’s rivals, meanwhile, have seized on the reported warning to renew their attacks on his handling of the events preceding October 7.
Gadi Eizenkot, currently polling as the prime minister’s main challenger in Israel’s upcoming elections, said Saturday that the revelation about the warning “leaves no room for doubt: Netanyahu led, with blindness, arrogance and irresponsibility, the State of Israel to the greatest disaster in its history.”
In May, Netanyahu’s office said the prime minister had secretly visited the UAE in March, during the early days of the Iran war, calling it a “historic breakthrough.” The UAE foreign ministry, however, denied his claim at the time as “completely unfounded.”
During the war, Israel is also said to have deployed an Iron Dome missile defense system to the UAE and Israeli officials have said security cooperation between the two countries reached unprecedented levels.
Netanyahu has never made a publicly acknowledged official visit to the UAE.

articles.title_orig: EU pushes China to accept import quotas in bid to rebalance trade
articles.title_zh: EU pushes China to accept import quotas in bid to rebalance trade
articles.content_orig:
Brussels and Beijing are fighting over quotas that would limit Chinese imports to the EU market, as the Europeans seek to rebalance their trade relationship with China, Euronews has learned.
Both started intense negotiations last June over EU and Chinese access to each other’s markets, with an October deadline set by the European Commission to reach "tanglible" results. However, China is pushing hard against the EU's attempts to protect its market.
According to one person familiar with the matter, the Commission, which is negotiating on behalf of the 27 EU countries on trade issues, wants China to accept quotas on specific products.
However, it is unclear how China would accept and respect such quotas.
According to media reports, so-called “voluntary export restrictions” have been pushed by the Commission for electric vehicles. But Beijing’s trade minister rejected them in a statement earlier this month.
If China accepted such a system of restrictions, it would mean that it voluntarily limits its exports to the EU on the basis of a deal negotiated with the Commission, sparing the EU from adopting defensive trade measures that might be seen as an aggressive move by China.
Technical negotiations are in their final stretch as the October deadline is approaching.
Director General of DG Trade at the Commission, Ditte Juul Jørgensen, travelled to China last week for two days of heated discussions, and EU Trade Commissioner Maroš Šefčovič is due to be in Beijing on 8 and 9 October for political talks, ahead of a key meeting of EU leaders in Brussels.
To give negotiations a chance, the Commission has delayed the adoption of trade defence mechanisms aiming to protect the EU chemical industry, according to another person familiar with the matter. The chemical industry is one of the sectors most threatened by Chinese competition in the EU.
However, the threat also targets other sectors, making the rebalancing of the trade relationship “existential” for the Europeans, EU Industry and Trade Commissioner Stéphane Séjourné told Euronews last week.
According to the Commission, the EU already lost 250,000 industrial jobs last year, particularly concentrated in energy-intensive sectors and automotive supply chains.

articles.title_orig: The Xbox Series X Can Now Play PlayStation 5 Games - Here's How
articles.title_zh: The Xbox Series X Can Now Play PlayStation 5 Games - Here's How
articles.content_orig:
Certain PlayStation 5 games are now running on Xbox Series X hardware thanks to a new emulator developed by the modding community. While the latest PS5 games, like "Marvel's Wolverine," won't be running on Xbox anytime soon, there's been a surprising amount of progress made with PS5 emulation on PC — and that progress is slowly being transferred to emulation on Xbox.
The root of this project is KytyPS5, an open-source PlayStation 5 emulator for PC. A modder named Devran Cosmo Uenal built a special port of the emulator for Xbox Series X, calling this new version PS5X. It's not quite up to par with KytyPS5 on PC, but the results are already impressive.
Multiple PS5 games are somewhat playable on PS5X, complete with Xbox inputs and a fancy user interface to swap between titles. The experience isn't perfect by any means, but they're semi-playable with minor glitches and performance problems — a remarkable achievement for experimental emulation in such an early state.
Currently, only a handful of small PS5 games are playable on PS5X. Uenal's YouTube page features a PS5X library with "Gex Trilogy," "Hellboy: Web of Wyrd," "Marvel Cosmic Invasion," and "Quake 2.' Smaller games like these are typically the first to reach playable states with new emulators, but things can improve fast. Just look at Nintendo Switch emulation on Android , for example.
PS5X is still in a very early state, and the gameplay footage recorded by Uenal shows "Quake 2" running at an inconsistent framerate, bouncing between 20 and 40 FPS. It's impressive that the PS5 version of "Quake 2" is running on Xbox hardware at all, but PS5X still needs a lot of work if it's going to run big PS5 exclusives like "Demon's Souls" or "Ghost of Yotei."
Work seems to be progressing quickly on PS5X, however. A new user interface update posted by Uenal shows "Crash Bandicoot 4: It's About Time," "Grand Theft Auto 5," and "Gran Turismo 7" as new additions to his library, indicating that these games are being tested. When PS5X releases publicly, you'll be able to install and test it yourself by putting your Xbox in developer mode. And don't worry — it's totally safe, and you won't brick your Xbox Series X by doing so.
PS5X is behind right now because KytyPS5 uses Vulkan rendering on PC, but the Xbox Series X doesn't support it. Everything has to be manually translated to DirectX to work on Xbox, which hurts compatibility and performance. If you're eager to test out PS5 emulation and you have a powerful gaming PC , you can check out KytyPS5 to get a sneak peek at some of the features and performance improvements that'll come to PS5X down the line.
KytyPS5 has made significant breakthroughs in recent months, and progress shows no signs of slowing down. "Astro Bot" and "Demon's Souls" can both run without crashing, and while the framerate dips down into the single digits, this is still an impressive achievement for PS5 emulation. Since PS5X is a port of KytyPS5, these advancements will likely come to PS5X later on if work continues on the project.
PlayStation 5 emulation continues to grow at a rapid pace on PC, meaning big games like "Grand Theft Auto 5" might be the next titles to run on PS5X. "GTA 5" is surprisingly playable on KytyPS5 with high-end PC hardware, and Uenal had the game installed on PS5X in his user interface showcase video. It'll just take time to optimize things specifically for the Xbox port of the emulator.

articles.title_orig: Inside the Trump campaign strategy to reverse Republicans’ dwindling hopes of winning the midterms
articles.title_zh: Inside the Trump campaign strategy to reverse Republicans’ dwindling hopes of winning the midterms
articles.content_orig:
The midterms mood among Donald Trump’s inner circle has soured as GOP candidates openly break with the president and his approval ratings hit an all-time low, prompting a largely unspoken but age-old question: How does an unpopular president best help his party keep control of Congress?
Trump advisers have privately acknowledged that there’s little expectation he can win over large numbers of independents and swing voters, which was part of his path to victory in critical states in 2024. And while they’re more concerned about losing control of the House, Republicans’ previous confidence that they can hold onto the Senate is dwindling by the day.
“It’s obviously going to be f***ing rough,” one Trump adviser told CNN, adding that they believe the best-case scenario is achieving what Democrats did in 2022, when under former President Joe Biden they narrowly lost control of the House but kept the Senate.
Still, Trump’s team is planning an aggressive campaign schedule for Trump and Vice President JD Vance in October in both battleground and deep-red states alike, multiple officials told CNN — as advisers believe their only hope at holding ground is increasing turnout, and the president can help with that.
“The system is built around what areas we need to goose turnout 2-3 points,” one operative told CNN.
In recent weeks, Trump’s senior advisers, including chief of staff Susie Wiles, put together a calendar that has Trump on the campaign trail for most days in October, though two administration officials said that not all stops had been confirmed. He is planning trips to Alabama and Oklahoma next week, but a GOP official said those were “outliers” in the travel strategy, which would focus more on battleground districts.
“He’ll be playing hard in Florida, Texas, Michigan and Ohio — he’ll be on the road just about every day in October campaigning. We’re leaving it all on the table,” the official added. However, even in more purple states, the plan is for Trump to go to more conservative areas, according to another official.
“I’ll be out there spending money, and helping every one of them get elected. I won most of these places, often by a landslide. MAGA, pretend I am on the ballot,” Trump wrote in a Monday morning Truth Social post commenting on Republicans’ chances in the midterms. “Don’t let them open your Borders, and allow crime to again flourish.”
Advisers also hope the Trump-Vance campaigning will help raise money as Republican groups — including Trump’s MAGA Inc. PAC — have begun hemorrhaging cash across the country. This week, the Senate Leadership Fund increased its spending in Texas to $100 million to support GOP Senate candidate Ken Paxton in a state they haven’t lost in decades, exposing the party’s fresh worries about the Senate.
And while one Republican operative said that the enormous sum was moving the needle in their direction “some,” it wasn’t clear it would be enough to reverse the strong political headwinds largely created by the president himself.
Asked if there was anything Republicans could do to change the tide, the operative replied: “Go back in time and never start the war with Iran.”
Republicans on the future of their party
Republicans in both purple territories and even some red districts have broken from Trump on issues ranging from the Iran War to the economy to immigration. Republican Mike Rogers, the Michigan Senate candidate in one of the most closely watched races this cycle, lamented in a recent ad that “Groceries cost too much. We have to bring prices down.”
“The war with Iran needs to end and end quickly,” Rogers said. “When it does, energy costs will plummet, but Michigan families can’t afford to wait for that to happen.”
That sentiment was echoed by the GOP’s Senate candidates in Iowa and Ohio. Other Republican lawmakers have voted to limit Trump’s war powers. House lawmakers in Florida and Texas have also criticized the administration on immigration. Several others have removed Trump references from campaign websites.
The GOP official involved in strategy brushed off concerns about candidates distancing from the president, saying “they need to run the races they need to run, and we’re obviously encouraging them to do what they need to do.”
In a sign of how potentially polarizing the president and his MAGA brand are right now, much of the money being spent by Trump’s PAC is coming through two newly formed groups with far less politically aligned names: No Going Back PAC Inc. and Safety & Affordability PAC Inc.
However, Trump’s political team still believes that his ability to drive turnout is one of Republicans’ greatest assets come November. While some Republicans have quietly expressed concerns about candidates in sensitive races appearing alongside Trump, one official brushed off the notion.
“The cake is already baked. There’s no getting away from Trump for these guys. So we have to lean into it,” the official said. “The left is going to attack [Republican candidates] as being close to Trump no matter what, so why not get the benefit out of it, which is max turnout.”
Multiple sources working on midterm strategy told CNN that Trump’s political operation was working off that central belief — that they could still win with enough turnout. In order to minimize the percent of “persuadable” voters that are needed, their thinking goes, it’s critical to get as many base voters to the polls as possible.
“It’s all a turnout game,” a GOP campaign official said. “From day one, the campaign committees and the president’s political operation have been sharing data to make sure we’re hammering the exact people we need to turn out.”
Sources noted that while this was not the traditional way to look at a midterm when a president’s approval ratings are so low, Trump has always been a different political animal who defies typical expectations.
But his advisers also privately acknowledge a major problem with that strategy: Trump isn’t just an incredible driver of enthusiasm for his own supporters; he’s also a strong driver of Democratic turnout.
“The issue with putting his name on the ballot is it could ultimately serve as a bigger driving force for Democratic voters who hate him,” the campaign official said.
White House spokesperson Davis Ingle said in a statement that Trump has “built one of the most robust coalitions in political history” and “the President understands how to communicate with them.”
“President Trump is the unequivocal leader, best messenger, and unmatched motivator for the Republican Party, and he is committed to maintaining Republican majorities in Congress,” Ingle added.
The White House and the president’s political apparatus view Vance as a crucial surrogate, and one that tends to stay far more on message compared to the president. Both men are seen as potentially doing more damage than good in certain swing districts, sources familiar with the discussions tell CNN.
The decision of where and when to send both men is driven directly by the massive data operation that the president’s political team has amassed, one that was fortified during Trump’s 2024 campaign and is now also being used by the Republican National Committee and the GOP’s House and Senate campaign arms.
